text.p: Turkish state banks' continuing cash demand ahead of mid-month public sector salary payments caused money rates to rise and the central bank to fund cash despite a 52 trillion lira surplus at the opening, bankers said.
The central bank lent 13.1 trillion lira to banks at 52 percent overnight, 35.3 trillion lira at 67 percent via tmrw/next and 900 billion lira at 68 percent via tmrw/week.
The average overnight money rate surged to 71.11 percent from Tuesday's 64.54 percent.

The overnight repo rates were volatile between 65 and 77 percent in the day as the central bank did not intervene in the repo market, bankers said. The average overnight repo rate edged lower to 72.07 percent from previous 72.96.
The liquidity surplus earlier in the day and the rising prospect of a new government created minor demand for bonds, but the yields remained in a narrow range between 99-100 percent.
"The rising probability of new coalition government excluding the Islamist Welfare Party caused political tension haunting the markets since mid-April to ease," a banker said.
The most active paper in the bond market was again April 22, 1998 which yielded 100.33 percent, compared to yesterday's 100.55 percent. Volume in others were relatively lower.

Former minister Yalim Erez from the conservative True Path Party (DYP) stepped up efforts this week on forming a secularist pact to exclude the ruling Islamists by holding a second round of talks with two opposition leaders on Tuesday.
A conservative and a left-wing opposition leader said they fully agreed on the new coalition proposal which Erez said would aim to rule rather than hold early elections.
Erez who is expected to meet a second left-wing leader this week, said he would also discuss the plan with deputy Prime Minister and DYP leader Tansu Ciller as soon as possible.

It is not clear how many DYP deputies will support Erez's move but conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz has said there was support within the party. Erez said the opposition planned to file a censure motion against the government if the DYP did not pull out of the government.
Turkish lira weakened against dollar to 137,390 lira from Tuesday's 137,000 close in line with the firmer dollar/mark parity and the cost of lira funding.

The lira's depreciation versus the central bank's foreign currency basket consisting 60 percent of marks and 40 percent of dollars reached 3.56 percent since beginning of May compared to last month's 3.36 percent.
